title: Conormal module generated by the codimension number of elements gives a global complete intersection nearby
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $S=P/I$ and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal. Let $d=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ be the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Then $d$ is an integer with $0\le d\le n$; and if the localization $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ of the $S$-module $I/I^2$ at $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] can be generated by $n-d$ elements as a module over the local ring $S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], then there is $g\in S$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the localization $S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), implication (3) => (1), where c = height(q') - height(q) = n - dim_q(S) by Lemma 00P2 (lemma-codimension); proof lines 35937-35985: first paragraph (generators of (I/I^2)_q lift to generators of I_{q'} by Nakayama 00DV, so (3) => (2)) and third paragraph ('We continue with the notation...': clearing denominators, g' with I_{g'} = (f'_1..f'_c), g'' with dim S_{g''} = n - c, S_g = k[x_1..x_{n+1}]/(f'_1..f'_c, x_{n+1}g'g''-1))

proof.text: Let $\pi:P\to S$ be the quotient map and $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime ideal of $P$ containing $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-at-point-height-difference], $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ and $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$ are integers with $0\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\le n$ and $d=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals $n-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')+\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$. Hence $d$ is an integer, $d\le n$ (as $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$) and $d\ge n-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')\ge0$. This is the first assertion. Put $c=n-d$, an integer with $0\le c\le n$, and assume from now on that $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ is generated over $S_{\mathfrak q}$ by $c$ elements.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci, line 35909), statement lines 35915-35918: c = height(q') - height(q), 'in other words dim_q(S) = n - c (see Lemma 00P2)'

proof.text: (Generators taken in $I$.) Let $m_1,\dots,m_c$ generate $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ over $S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Write $m_j=(a_j+I^2)/s_j$ with $a_j\in I$ and $s_j\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$. Since $s_j$ is a unit of $S_{\mathfrak q}$, the elements $(a_j+I^2)/1=s_j m_j$ ($j=1,\dots,c$) also generate $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$. Put $f'_j=a_j\in I\subseteq P$ and $J=(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)\subseteq I$, an ideal of $P$. (This is the source's choice of $f_1,\dots,f_c\in I_{\mathfrak q'}$ generating $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ followed by its clearing of denominators $f'_i=d_if_i$, done at once.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC, lines 35944-35945 ('Let f_1, ..., f_c in I_{q'} be elements which generate (I/I^2)_q') and lines 35967-35970 (d_i not in q' with f'_i = d_i f_i in k[x_1..x_n])

proof.text: (Nakayama: $IR=JR$.) Let $R=P_{\mathfrak q'}$, a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak q'R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $M=IR$, $N=JR\subseteq M$ the ideals of $R$ generated by the $a/1$, $a\in I$, resp. by the $f'_j/1$. $P$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so $I=(b_1,\dots,b_m)$ is finitely generated and $M$ is the finitely generated $R$-module generated by $b_1/1,\dots,b_m/1$. Claim: $M=N+\mathfrak mM$. It suffices to show $a/1\in N+\mathfrak mM$ for $a\in I$, since $M$ is generated by these. By step 2, $(a+I^2)/1=\sum_j(\beta_j/t)\,(a_j+I^2)/1$ in $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ for some $\beta_j\in S$ and one $t\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ (common denominator); by the equality criterion of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] there is $u\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $u\bigl(t(a+I^2)-\sum_j\beta_j(a_j+I^2)\bigr)=0$ in $I/I^2$. Choose $\tilde u,\tilde t,\tilde\beta_j\in P$ with $\pi(\tilde u)=u$, $\pi(\tilde t)=t$, $\pi(\tilde\beta_j)=\beta_j$; then $\tilde u,\tilde t\notin\mathfrak q'$ and, since $S$ acts on $I/I^2$ through $P$, $e:=\tilde u\tilde t a-\sum_j\tilde u\tilde\beta_jf'_j\in I^2$. In $R$: $a/1=(\tilde u\tilde t)^{-1}\bigl(\sum_j(\tilde u\tilde\beta_j/1)(f'_j/1)+e/1\bigr)\in N+I^2R$, and $I^2R=(IR)(IR)\subseteq\mathfrak q'R\cdot M=\mathfrak mM$ because $I\subseteq\mathfrak q'$. So $M=N+\mathfrak mM$: the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak mM$ is all of $M/\mathfrak mM$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] (its submodule form) $N=M$, i.e. $IR=(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC, lines 35945-35946 ('By Lemma 00DV (lemma-NAK) we see that f_1, ..., f_c generate I_{q'}') and line 35970 ('Then it is still true that I_{q'} = (f'_1, ..., f'_c)R'); Lemma 00DV (lemma-NAK, line 3620), item with I = rad(R) = m; tags 00SC, 00DV verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: (The element $g'$.) With $I=(b_1,\dots,b_m)$ as in step 3: each $b_i/1\in IR=JR$, so, with a common denominator, $b_i/1=\sum_j(r_{ij}/s_i)(f'_j/1)$ with $r_{ij}\in P$, $s_i\in P\setminus\mathfrak q'$; by the equality criterion of $R=P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] there is $u_i\in P\setminus\mathfrak q'$ with $u_i(s_ib_i-\sum_jr_{ij}f'_j)=0$, so $u_is_ib_i\in J$. Put $g'=\prod_iu_is_i$; $g'\notin\mathfrak q'$ since $\mathfrak q'$ is prime, and $g'b_i\in J$ for all $i$, hence $g'I\subseteq J\subseteq I$. (This is the source's '$I_{g'}=(f'_1,\dots,f'_c)$': after inverting $g'$, $I$ and $J$ generate the same ideal; the finiteness of the generating set $b_1,\dots,b_m$ uses that $P$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC, lines 35971-35972 ('Hence there exists a g' in k[x_1..x_n], g' not in q' such that I_{g'} = (f'_1, ..., f'_c)')

proof.text:
(The element $g''$.) By the definition of $d=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $\mathfrak q$ in $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $\dim U=d$ (subspace topology [def-kun-subspace-topology], Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]). The sets $D(h)$, $h\in S$, form a basis of the topology of $\operatorname{Spec}S$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (i), so there is $h\in S$ with $\mathfrak q\in D(h)\subseteq U$. Choose $g''\in P$ with $\pi(g'')=h$; then $g''
otin\mathfrak q'$. Put $h_0=g'g''\in P$ and $g=\pi(h_0)=\pi(g')h\in S$; $g
otin\mathfrak q$ because $g'
otin\mathfrak q'$, $g''
otin\mathfrak q'$ and $\mathfrak q'$ is prime. So $\mathfrak q\in D(g)=D(\pi(g'))\cap D(h)\subseteq D(h)\subseteq U$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC, lines 35973-35976 ('pick g'' not in q' such that dim(S_{g''}) = dim_q Spec(S) ... set g equal to the image of g'g'' in S'); Topology, Definition 0055 (topology.tex, definition-Krull, line 1392) item (4) and the remark after it (line 1421), tag 0055 verified

proof.text: ($\dim S_g=n-c$.) $D(g)$ and $D(h)$ are open neighbourhoods of $\mathfrak q$ with $D(g)\subseteq D(h)\subseteq U$. By the definition of $d$ as a minimum over open neighbourhoods [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $d\le\dim D(g)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone], $\dim D(g)\le\dim D(h)\le\dim U=d$. Hence $\dim D(g)=d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] (ii), $\operatorname{Spec}S_g\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ is a homeomorphism onto $D(g)$; a homeomorphism maps closed irreducible subsets to closed irreducible subsets and preserves strict inclusions, both ways, so it preserves the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Therefore $\dim S_g=\dim\operatorname{Spec}S_g=d=n-c$ (in the notation of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field], $\dim T$ is the Krull dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}T$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC, lines 35974-35975 and 35983 ('by our choice of g'' this ring has dimension n - c'), with the remark after Topology, Definition 0055 (topology.tex line 1421: U' subset U open implies dim(U') <= dim(U))

proof.text: (The presentation.) Let $A=P/J$ and $r\in A$ the class of $h_0$. (a) The surjection $\rho:A=P/J\to P/I=S$ (as $J\subseteq I$) sends $r$ to $g$, so it induces a $k$-algebra map $\rho_r:A_r\to S_g$, $(x+J)/r^m\mapsto\pi(x)/g^m$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]; it is surjective, as every element of $S_g$ is $\pi(x)/g^m$. It is injective: if $\pi(x)/g^m=0$ then $g^l\pi(x)=0$ for some $l$, i.e. $h_0^lx\in I$; then $g'h_0^lx\in J$ by step 4, so $h_0^{l+1}x=g''\cdot g'h_0^lx\in J$, i.e. $r^{l+1}(x+J)=0$ and $(x+J)/r^m=0$ in $A_r$. So $A_r\cong S_g$. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient] (with its $R=A$, its $r$ our $r$), $A[x_{n+1}]/(rx_{n+1}-1)\cong A_r$ as $A$-algebras. (c) Reducing coefficients modulo $J$ gives a surjection $P[x_{n+1}]\to A[x_{n+1}]$ whose kernel is $JP[x_{n+1}]$ (the polynomials with all coefficients in $J$) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; composing with the quotient by $(rx_{n+1}-1)$, whose preimage is $h_0x_{n+1}-1$ modulo $JP[x_{n+1}]$, gives $k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f'_1,\dots,f'_c,\,h_0x_{n+1}-1)\cong A[x_{n+1}]/(rx_{n+1}-1)$. Together: $S_g\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f'_1,\dots,f'_c,\,x_{n+1}g'g''-1)$ as $k$-algebras, a quotient of a polynomial ring in $n+1$ variables by $c+1$ polynomials.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00SC, lines 35976-35982 ('S_g = k[x_1..x_n, x_{n+1}]/(f'_1, ..., f'_c, x_{n+1}g'g'' - 1)'); the identification B[x]/(gx - 1) = B_g as in the proof of Lemma 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL, line 35632) and of Lemma 00SA (lemma-localize-lci)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By step 7, $S_g\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(F_1,\dots,F_{c+1})$ with $F_j=f'_j$ for $j\le c$ and $F_{c+1}=x_{n+1}h_0-1$, and by step 6, $\dim S_g=n-c=(n+1)-(c+1)$. By part (1) of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] (with its integers $n+1$, $c+1\ge0$), $S_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$; and $g\notin\mathfrak q$ by step 5.

lean.statement: theorem conormal_generators_global_complete_intersection (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I)) [q.IsPrime] : ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDimAt (⟨q, inferInstance⟩ : PrimeSpectrum (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I)) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ d ≤ n ∧ ((∃ gens : Fin (n - d) → LocalizedModule q.primeCompl (Ideal.Cotangent I), Submodule.span (R := Localization.AtPrime q) (Set.range gens) = ⊤) → ∃ g : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I), g ∉ q ∧ IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g))
